source_text: ρηκότες δὲ ἤδη, καὶ, καθάπερ ἐγᾦμαι, διαρκῶς τὰ ἐπί τε τῇ βύσσῳ καὶ τῇ πορφύρᾳ, καὶ τῷ κεκλωσμένῳ κοκκίνῳ, καὶ μέν τοι καὶ ὑακίνθῳ, παρωσόμεθα μὲν τὸ ταυτοεπές· ἐκεῖνό γε μὴν ἐροῦμεν εἰς τὸ παρόν· Τὸ καταπέτασμα τὸ ἐπὶ τεσσάρων στύλων χρυσῶν, ὧν αἱ βάσεις ἀργυραῖ, τὸ Χριστοῦ μυστήριον ὑπεδήλου τότε. Τί γάρ; οὐχὶ καταπέτασμα τὸ σῶμα Χριστοῦ καὶ σοφὸς ἡμῖν ὠνόμασε Παῦλος, οὕτω λέγων, «Ἣν ἐνεκαίνισεν ἡμῖν ὁδὸν πρόσφατον καὶ ζῶσαν διὰ τοῦ καταπετάσματος, τουτέστι, τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ;» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὀρθῶς ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἄθρει δὴ οὖν ὡς ἐν σκιαῖς καὶ αἰνίγμασιν, ὅτι Θεὸς ὢν καὶ ἐκ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς κατὰ φύσιν ὁ Λόγος, ὡς ἐν χρυσῇ καὶ ἀσήπτῳ γέγονε κιβωτῷ, τῷ ἐκ Παρθένου ναῷ· ἄσηπτον γὰρ καὶ τίμιον τὸ σῶμα Χριστοῦ· μονονουχὶ δὲ καὶ ἐκρύπτετο καθάπερ ἐν τάξει καταπετάσματος, τὴν σάρκα λαβών· κρύπτεσθαι δέ φαμεν τὸν ἐκ Θεοῦ Λόγον, οὐχ ὡς ἐν βραχεῖ περιορισθέντα σώματι· πανταχῆ γὰρ καὶ ἐν πᾶσιν ὁ Υἱός· ἀλλὰ τῷ λανθάνειν οἰκονομικῶς, καὶ τὸν τῆς ἀναδείξεως ὑπομένειν καιρόν. Ἀναδείξεως δὲ τῆς εἰς ἅπαντας ὁ καιρὸς, ἡ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναβίωσις. Πρὸ μὲν γὰρ τοῦ τιμίου σταυροῦ, τοῖς ἁγίοις ἐπέταττε μαθηταῖς, ἵνα μὴ φανερὸν αὐτὸν ποιῶσι. Γέγραπται γὰρ ὡδί. Μετὰ δέ γε τὸ ἀναβιῶναι παθόντα τὸν θάνατον, «Πορευθέντες, φησὶ, μαθητεύσατε πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, βαπτίζοντες αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Πατρὸς, καὶ τοῦ Υἱοῦ, καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος.» Οὐκοῦν ἐπεκρέματο μὲν τοῖς στύλοις τὸ καταπέτασμα, κατακαλύπτον ἔσω τὴν κιβωτὸν, τύπος δ' ἂν εἴη Χριστοῦ, τοῖς τῶν ἁγίων εὐαγγελιστῶν κηρύγμασιν αἰρομένου τε ὑψοῦ, καὶ ἐν δόξῃ θεότητος ὁρωμένου τοῖς ἐν τῇ ἁγίᾳ σκηνῇ, τουτέστι, τῇ Ἐκκλησίᾳ. Τέσσαρες δὲ οἱ στύλοι, χρυσοῖ καὶ περιάργυροι· ἰσάριθμοι δὲ αὐτοῖς οἱ εὐαγγελισταὶ, λαμπροί τε καὶ τίμιοι. Οὐκοῦν ἔκειτο μὲν ἡ κιβωτὸς, ἄνωθεν δὲ κάτω διῆκον τὸ καταπέτασμα, τὸ ἐκ βύσσου καὶ πορφύρας καὶ τῶν ἄλλων, οὐχ ὁρατὴν ἐτίθει. Ἄνωθεν δὲ τοῦ καταπετάσματος καὶ τῶν εἰς δεξιά τε καὶ εὐώνυμα Χερουβὶμ, ἐχρημάτιζε Θεὸς, δεικνὺς ὅτι καὶ ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν κτίσιν ἐστί· καὶ αὐτὰ δὲ πάντα τὰ τῶν λογικῶν ἀνωτάτω, τουτέστι τὰ Σεραφὶμ, τὴν θείαν τε καὶ ἄῤῥητον ὑποκάθηται δόξαν, καὶ αὐτὸν δορυφοροῦντα τὸν Υἱὸν, εἰ καὶ γέγονε σὰρξ, καὶ ὡς ἐν ὑφέσει τυχὸν τῆς πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα ἰσότητος, καθὸ πέφυκεν ἄνθρωπος. Τοιγάρτοι καὶ ἔφασκεν αὐτός· «Ὁ Πατήρ μου μείζων μού ἐστιν.» Ἶσος δὲ ὢν κατὰ φύσιν τῷ γεγεννηκότι, τὸ ἐν μείοσι γενέσθαι φησὶ διὰ μόνον τὸ ἀνθρώπινον. Διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἐν τῇ ἁγίᾳ σκηνῇ, κύκλῳ μὲν τοῦ καταπετάσματος, τὰ Χερουβὶμ, καὶ αὐτὰ ὡς Θεὸν δορυφοροῦντα τὸν Υἱόν. Καὶ μὴν καὶ αὐτοῦ τοῦ καταπετάσματος ἄνωθεν, ὃ ἦν εἰς τύπον Χριστοῦ, νοεῖται Θεός. «Καὶ γνωσθήσομαι» γὰρ, φησὶν, «ἐκεῖθεν, καὶ λαλήσω σοι.» Ἐπέκεινα γὰρ πάσης κτίσεως ὁ Πατὴρ, καὶ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Ἐμμανουὴλ, οὐ καθ' ὃ νοεῖται καὶ ἔστι Θεός· ἶσος γάρ ἐστι κατὰ πάντα Θεῷ· ἀλλ' ὅσον
pass_a_gloss: [Εἰ]ρηκότες: Having spoken already and, as I think, sufficiently (διαρκῶς) the things about the linen and the purple and the spun scarlet and indeed the hyacinth, we will push aside (παρωσόμεθα) the repetition (τὸ ταυτοεπές); but this we will say for the present: the veil upon four golden pillars, whose bases are silver, was hinting (ὑπεδήλου) then the mystery (μυστήριον) of Christ. For what? Did not wise Paul also name the body of Christ a veil for us, saying: Which (way) he inaugurated (ἐνεκαίνισεν) for us, a way fresh (πρόσφατον) and living, through the veil, that is, his flesh (σάρξ)? PALL.: You said rightly. CYR.: Observe (ἄθρει) then as in shadows (σκιαί) and riddles (αἰνίγματα), that being God and from God the Father according to nature (κατὰ φύσιν), the Word (Λόγος) has come to be as in a golden and undecaying (ἀσήπτῳ) ark, the temple (ναός) from the Virgin (Παρθένος); for undecaying and precious (τίμιον) is the body of Christ; and he was all but (μονονουχί) also hidden as in the rank/position (τάξις) of a veil, having taken the flesh. We say the Word from God is hidden, not as circumscribed (περιορισθέντα) in a small body; for the Son is everywhere and in all; but by escaping notice (λανθάνειν) economically (οἰκονομικῶς), and awaiting (ὑπομένειν) the time of showing-forth (ἀνάδειξις). The time of showing-forth to all is the coming-back-to-life (ἀναβίωσις) from the dead. For before the precious cross he commanded (ἐπέταττε) the holy disciples that they not make him manifest (φανερόν). For it is written thus. But after coming back to life having suffered death: Going, he says, make disciples (μαθητεύσατε) of all the nations, baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. So the veil was hanging on (ἐπεκρέματο) the pillars, covering the ark inside; it would be a type (τύπος) of Christ, lifted (αἰρομένου) on high by the proclamations (κηρύγματα) of the holy evangelists and seen in glory of Godhead (θεότης) by those in the holy tent, that is, the Church. Four the pillars, golden and silver-surrounded (περιάργυροι); equal in number to them the evangelists, bright and precious. So the ark lay, and the veil reaching (διῆκον) from above downward, of linen and purple and the rest, made it not visible. Above the veil and the cherubim at right and left God gave oracles (ἐχρημάτιζε), showing that he is above all creation (κτίσις); and all the highest of rational beings (λογικοί), that is the Seraphim, sit beneath (ὑποκάθηται) the divine and ineffable (ἄρρητον) glory, and escort as bodyguard (δορυφοροῦντα) the Son himself, even if he became flesh, and as in a lowering (ὕφεσις), perhaps (τυχόν), of the equality (ἰσότης) toward the Father, inasmuch as (καθό) he is (πέφυκεν) man. Therefore he himself also said: My Father is greater than I. Being equal (ἶσος) by nature to the one who begot (γεγεννηκότι) him, he says the being among lesser things (ἐν μείοσι) on account of only the human (τὸ ἀνθρώπινον). On account of this also in the holy tent, around the veil, the cherubim, they too escorting the Son as God. And indeed above the veil itself, which was for a type of Christ, God is understood (νοεῖται). For: And I will be made known, he says, from there, and I will speak to you. For the Father is beyond (ἐπέκεινα) all creation and of Emmanuel himself, not according as he is understood and is God, for he is equal in all things to God, but insofar as (ἀλλ' ὅσον) [§8: he came into the form of a servant and the measure of humanity].
pass_b_english: Cyril: We have already spoken, and sufficiently, I think, about the linen and the purple, the twisted scarlet, and the blue as well, so we will set repetition aside. But this much we will say for the present: the veil on four golden pillars with silver bases was then a hint of the mystery of Christ. Why so? Did not the wise Paul also name the body of Christ a veil for us, when he said: ‘the new and living way which he opened for us through the veil, that is, his flesh’ (Hebrews 10:20)?

Cyril: See, then, as in shadows and riddles, how the Word, who is God and from God the Father by nature, came to be as in a golden and incorruptible ark, that is, in the temple taken from the Virgin; for the body of Christ is incorruptible and precious. And by taking the flesh he was all but hidden, as though behind a veil. We say that the Word from God was hidden, not as though he were confined within a small body, for the Son is everywhere and in all things, but because he remained unnoticed, in keeping with the plan of salvation, and waited for the time of his showing forth. And the time of his showing forth to all was his return to life from the dead. For before the precious cross he ordered the holy disciples not to make him known (Matthew 16:20); so it is written. But after he had suffered death and come back to life, he says: ‘Go and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit’ (Matthew 28:19). So the veil hung on the pillars, covering the ark within; and it would be a type of Christ, who is lifted up on high by the preaching of the holy evangelists and is seen in the glory of the Godhead by those in the holy tent, that is, in the Church. The pillars are four, golden and set in silver; and the evangelists are equal to them in number, bright and precious. So the ark lay there, and the veil of linen and purple and the rest, reaching from top to bottom, kept it out of sight. Above the veil and above the cherubim on the right and on the left, God uttered his oracles, showing that he is above all creation. Even the highest of all rational beings, that is, the Seraphim, are seated beneath the divine glory beyond words, and they attend the Son himself as his guard of honor, even though he became flesh (John 1:14) and, insofar as he is man, came perhaps into a kind of lowering of his equality with the Father. That is why he himself said: ‘My Father is greater than I’ (John 14:28). Yet being equal by nature to the One who begot him, he says that he came into a lesser state, and this only because of his humanity. For this reason, in the holy tent too, the cherubim were around the veil, they too attending the Son as God. And above the veil itself, which stood as a type of Christ, God is understood to be. For he says: ‘And I will make myself known from there, and I will speak with you’ (Exodus 25:22). anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril, De adoratione Book 10. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withheld earlier English was not used.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens with the participle Εἰρηκότες split at the column break (Εἰ- at the end of §6); translated whole here. Hebrews 10:20 is quoted as Paul’s, following Cyril’s attribution. ‘He ordered the holy disciples not to make him known’: the sense matches Matthew 16:20 (also Mark 8:30, Luke 9:21), cited there; the wording ἵνα μὴ φανερὸν αὐτὸν ποιῶσι echoes Matthew 12:16 and Mark 3:12, where the command is to the crowds and the spirits. ‘For it is written thus’ (Γέγραπται γὰρ ὡδί) is followed by no quotation in the PG text; a quotation may have dropped out, or the phrase may simply point to the Gospel account. Rendered ‘so it is written’ and nothing is supplied. ‘The temple taken from the Virgin’ may recall John 2:21 and ‘incorruptible body’ Psalm 16:10 / Acts 2:27; both too loose to cite. ‘Seraphim’ is Cyril’s word here (not ‘cherubim’), kept; the image may recall Isaiah 6:2, not cited. ‘He became flesh’ is John 1:14. ὡς ἐν ὑφέσει τυχὸν τῆς πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα ἰσότητος, καθὸ πέφυκεν ἄνθρωπος: Cyril hedges twice (ὡς, τυχόν) and limits the lowering to the humanity; Pass B keeps ‘perhaps’, ‘a kind of’ and ‘insofar as he is man’. ‘My Father is greater than I’ is John 14:28 (Cyril adds μου). Possible echo of Philippians 2:6 in ‘equal by nature’, not cited. ‘I will make myself known from there, and I will speak with you’ is Exodus 25:22 LXX (also Exodus 30:6). ἐχρημάτιζε rendered ‘gave his answers’ (oracular speech). οἰκονομικῶς rendered ‘in keeping with the plan of salvation’. The section ends mid-sentence at ἀλλ’ ὅσον; §8 continues ‘he came into the form of a servant and the measure of humanity’ (Philippians 2:7, to be cited in §8). Pass B therefore ends with ‘but insofar as’ and no full stop.

changes: removed leading ellipsis: §7 begins a new sentence (the split participle Εἰρηκότες is translated whole)
ἀσήπτῳ κιβωτῷ: 'ark that does not decay' -> 'incorruptible ark', matching 'incorruptible' for the body in the next clause (same word)
'when he took the flesh' -> 'by taking the flesh' (participle gives the means of the hiding)
'stood perhaps in a kind of lowering from his equality' -> 'came perhaps into a kind of lowering of his equality' (no added verb 'stood'; hedges ὡς/τυχόν and limit καθὸ πέφυκεν ἄνθρωπος kept)
τὸ ἐν μείοσι γενέσθαι: 'speaks of being in a lesser state' -> 'says that he came into a lesser state, and this only because of his humanity' (aorist kept; 'only' scoped to the cause)
citations checked: Hebrews 10:20, Matthew 16:20, Matthew 28:19, John 1:14, John 14:28, Exodus 25:22 (LXX 25:21 in some editions; English 25:22) - all correct; Seraphim kept as in Cyril's text
